corrections.after:
Ikra creates an Abyssal Bubble that Slows Enemies by 20% while they are in its radius.

The Bubble can be popped by hitting it with either Fathom or Brine, dealing 35/45/55/65/75 (+15%) magical damage to all Targets in a 520 Unit radius and restoring 30 Mana.

The Bubble amplifies after 1.1s, increasing the damage dealt to 75/120/165/210/255 (+80%) magical damage whilst Slowing all Targets hit by 40/45/50/55/60% for 1s.

Popping a Bubble with Brine deals Brine's Damage as well as Hydroclasm's Damage. If the Bubble is amplified when popped by Brine, the total damage penetrates 40% of the Target's Magical Armor.

Max Charges: 2

definition_review.scope: Main-game mechanics. All published articles from 1.14 through 1.16.4 and their embedded updates were checked. ARAM, Nitro, and Brawl-specific changes are excluded.

description_reviews.reason: The notes give a 15.5–91.5% range and +4.5% per level. Those endpoints do not reconcile across 18 levels. The published range is retained, but no per-level table has been invented.

The source differs from the 1.16 release description in the third-rank base damage and the flat empowered-hit damage. The explicit 1.16.1 target-health change is corrected, but the other discrepancies remain unverified.

errors.detail: 31 teammate entries involve heroes that have no statz hero page in this bracket (Wukong, Yurei), so no baseline exists and those pairs are not ranked.
hero-wide figures (hero-wide win rate, pairs, hero-wide matchups, ban rate) come from a pool about 1.7x the games on the Gold+ tier list; statz does not state what the extra games are
Partly verified descriptions: Frost Snap, Harmonic Currents, Mending. Conflicting fields remain explicitly unverified; inspect the blessing details.

Missing or incompatible Statz descriptions: Adaptive Plating, Arcane Resonance, Bio-Mechanical Fusion, Blood Bank, Cursed Corrupted, Dampening, Frost Snap, Growing Threat, Inescapable, Mana Siphon, Omnipresent, Roses, The Maw, Tri-Core, Voracity. 14 reviewed descriptions, 1 partly verified descriptions, and 0 unavailable. Build samples remain unchanged. Inspect Sources & accuracy or the perk details.

augment_review.method: Every selected default augment has an exact-description, named-ability review. Explicit capability changes and execution context are distinct. This is not a damage/cooldown simulator or an assumption about enemy loadouts.

build_advice.name: Protect the first decisive channel
build_advice.text: This is the protected-channel default, trading early flat penetration for survival of the channel. The bracelet only grants control immunity while its shield holds; damage or anti-shield can remove that protection. Against little interrupt pressure, buy Wraith Leggings earlier.

build_advice.name: Separate clear from catch utility
build_advice.text: Dynamo requires the immobilizing catch and allied damage during its short window. Overlord remains a farming/health-stacking alternative when you are not the sole initiator; do not buy both clear engines automatically while the next objective needs armor and catch utility.

build_advice.name: Serath: finishing chain versus a marked duel
build_advice.text: Weald is the default for this attack-speed/on-hit finishing plan: current Pred.gg Jungle observations favor it over the retained Thraex alternative, but these are separate conditional samples, not a causal test. Dryad’s Boon supports repeated basic-ability access; Wind-Rider follows the actual teleport/leap entry. Weald needs a low-health target and has a per-target cooldown; it does not amplify every attack. Keep Thraex for a deliberately sustained marked-target duel.

build_advice.name: Carry buffs must fit the firing pattern
build_advice.text: Marshal fits repeated basic attacks. Revenant’s burst and Legion’s attack-speed conversion require their own item interpretation; do not buy a generic support aura simply because the ally occupies Carry.

guidance.build_method: 85 individually reviewed hero/role starting plans cover all 54 heroes. Kit interactions determine the playstyle; current official changes and versioned catalogs constrain mechanics. The final three slots are adaptable examples. No rate proves a universal best build. Disputed fields are excluded from decisions, and samples with different cohorts are never combined.

builds.author: Codex editorial review
builds.caution: Tyrant of Thorns removes Royal Flourish’s control. Dynamo needs the root from Imperial Lash or Queen’s Garden instead. Burn damage pushes the wave; do not let passive clear drag you past safe vision.

item_notes.reason: Burn supplies nearby wave pressure while Royal Flourish is cycling. Health also supports her true-damage scaling; this is not permission to ignore the lane’s damage type.
Physical armor and health support a committed catch. Its damage window comes from Lash or Garden immobilization, not the mesmerize removed by Tyrant of Thorns.
Magical defense helps hold the garden while nearby allied magical damage benefits from the aura. Adele’s own true damage is not amplified by a magical-damage aura.
Health and magical armor support Iron Rose’s defensive job. The extra armor requires being immobilized; it is not permanently active.
Health supports her health-scaled damage. After the item builds its combat stacks, land the empowered basic attack for its damage and heal instead of treating it as a spell proc.
Heavy physical defense is for sustained attack pressure. Iron Rose uses both armor types; replace this late physical slot when magical threats are the actual problem.

builds.title: Hold space for the next damage window
builds.why: Trade behind Iron Rose, then use Imperial Lash or Queen’s Garden to create the damage window. Tyrant of Thorns makes this a durable close-range pressure plan; Royal Flourish supplies damage and movement, not mesmerize. Keep the wave in a position that your jungler can reach.

builds.author: Codex editorial review
builds.caution: A long Lash can separate you from the carry. Frosted Lure and Tainted Charm need sustained proximity. Replace the anti-heal flex item when healing is not a problem; this is not a six-item shopping order for every match.

item_notes.reason: Lash and Flourish can immobilize, opening Dynamo’s brief damage-amplification window.
You already fight close to the target; the delayed proximity effect rewards staying there, not a single drive-by.
Protect nearby allies with both armors while holding the front. Its aura does not follow an ally outside range.
Apply anti-heal by remaining near the affected enemy, independent of magical damage. This is a flex answer, not assumed enemy healing.
Use the magical armor against a real magic threat; the triggered armor bonus requires being immobilized.
Longer engagements can justify recovery and health after the affordable team tools. Move an actual matchup defense ahead of it.

builds.title: Hold the catch while your ally supplies damage
builds.why: Imperial Lash and Royal Flourish create the opening. Build affordable durability so Iron Rose and Queen’s Garden keep you in contact while allies use Crown of Thorns. Your kit deals physical and true damage; a caster anti-heal item is a poor default application plan.

builds.author: Codex editorial review
builds.caution: This is a mixed-damage tank plan, not a physical-power build. Fireballs lose effectiveness against repeated hits on one target. Do not spend both web movements entering a fight with no exit. Raiment’s missing-health recovery is out of combat.

item_notes.reason: Cast, then land the empowered attack for camp damage and a gank slow. Haste also supports Hellfire’s projectile count; Elafrost does not proc on every fireball.
Permanent and purchased health support the bite/execute identity. Fist converts that health into a periodic magical attack and heal, not physical power.
Stay near the rooted target to amplify Hellfire and allied magic damage. Buy its magical armor when that threat exists.
A deep web entry exposes you to control. The bonus armors require being immobilized; this does not prevent the execute channel being interrupted.
Health supports the bite while out-of-combat recovery lets you reset between objective attempts. It is not a second combat heal.
A late answer to physical damage while committing to the catch. Replace it when the dangerous enemy instead deals magical or true damage.

builds.title: Catch from terrain, survive the full channel
builds.why: Use Web Lash from terrain to start behind a lane’s escape route. Elafrost supplies mana regeneration and haste for repeated casts; Hellfire also scales its projectile count with haste. Health supports the bite and execute plan. Rotate with an ally who can hold the target while the ultimate channels.

builds.author: Codex editorial review
builds.caution: This is a health-and-defense plan with mixed kit damage, not physical-power stacking. Consume requires continued contact and can be interrupted. Void Helm supports real self-healing; anti-heal still reduces that recovery.

item_notes.reason: Health supports Maw and nearby burn helps clear. Match the first armor component to the opponent rather than assuming every offlaner deals physical damage.
The large health pool supports Maw and later healing opportunities. Its empowered basic attack needs four combat stacks; casting Consume does not trigger it by itself.
Magical defense and a nearby magical-damage aura support Hellfire and Consume’s pull damage. The physical bite and execute are different damage components.
Health and magical armor help survive long enough to reach Awakened. The immobilization-triggered armor increase remains conditional.
The healing increase directly supports Maw and Consume’s bite healing. Buy it sooner against magic pressure, but do not count it as protection from anti-heal.
Physical armor addresses repeated attacks during the committed frontline job. It provides no equivalent magical-damage mitigation.

builds.review_scope: Cross-source role review: current role evidence, economy, six purchase reasons, kit delivery, selected loadout, counterplay and composition job. Conditional source build rates are not full-build win probabilities.
builds.rune_note: Regenerative Tissue supports recovery between lane trades. Cannibalism rewards takedown participation. Predator requires camp-leader kills, so it remains a deliberate jungle-route option rather than the lane default. Both selected blessings fit their Krix slots.
builds.title: Hold space for the next damage window
builds.why: Use Crushing Maw for a short lane trade and heal, then retreat before Hunger expires if you cannot stay in range. Health supports Maw and Consume; keep Web Lash available for the enemy jungler or a safe wall exit. After shoving safely, bring a reachable target into allied damage.

builds.author: Codex editorial review
builds.caution: Repeated projectiles do not bypass item cooldowns. The crystal can move both enemies and allies, so its placement matters. Bring Spellbreaker forward when a single interrupt prevents you delivering the channel.

item_notes.reason: Mana and haste support the sustained Shredder cast; stack Azure through farm rather than assuming its completed bonus immediately.
Repeated ability damage fits Entropy’s short per-ability trigger interval and the kit’s stacking pressure; it is not an unlimited proc per projectile.
Power, flat penetration and movement support the low-health beam finish. The extra item damage is conditional on target health.
Magical penetration answers armor on the target you can reach. Buying it does not guarantee repeated beam hits.

Omnivamp and health-based damage support the cast/attack trade. The ability-triggered portion applies once per ability, not to every repeated hit.
Magical defense and a low-health cleanse help survive the channel or dash commitment. Save movement rather than relying only on the trigger.
Close-range physical armor and reduction suit fighting on a marked target. Ranged empowered attacks outside the aura do not carry its debuff with them.
The emergency shield creates time to meet the spin’s healing condition. It cannot supply a missing mark or a reset by itself.

builds.title: Prepare Soul Rip before committing the reset
builds.why: Use the projectiles or pull to mark a target, then alternate empowered attacks with the spin and dash. Augmentation matches those cast/attack windows, while Basilisk and Mutilator support sustained physical pressure. An allied catch lets you establish the mark without spending the dash as a blind entry.

builds.author: Codex editorial review
builds.caution: Out-of-combat recovery is not combat lifesteal. Hold the shield for a damage window and its stun rather than using it only as filler. A trapped enemy can still fight back, and allies must be in range to turn containment into a kill.

item_notes.reason: The dash enables the empowered attack and slow, while fog-wall movement helps approach. The short attack window still has to be used.
Attack between spear and shield casts to convert the proc. Repeated quick casts do not bypass its cooldown.
Repeated physical hits reduce armor during the arena duel. A single spear does not grant the full reduction.
Proximity armor reduction supports a physical ally firing into the arena while the armor helps you remain there.
Magical armor and a low-health cleanse help against counter-control after the arena entry. This is not a manual answer to every stun.
The shield can bridge a dangerous low-health trade; passive recovery only resumes out of combat. Change this flex slot when the threat calls for a different defense.

builds.review_scope: Cross-source role review: current role evidence, economy, six purchase reasons, kit delivery, selected loadout, counterplay and composition job. Conditional source build rates are not full-build win probabilities.
builds.rune_note: Authored for the stated kit and role. Blessings are checked against their Eternal and slot. Disputed blessing triggers are excluded from default plans; no whole-loadout win rate is inferred.
builds.title: Create a reachable arena, then stay on the trapped target
builds.why: Approach through fog, use the dash to prepare the Axe attack, and connect spear damage with attacks between casts. Place the arena where your mid or carry can actually contribute. Permanent power requires a kill inside that arena; a defensive cast to peel can still be correct without earning stacks.

builds.author: Codex editorial review
builds.caution: The thrown Spear’s extra damage requires the target below its health threshold. Alpha’s Court is inactive when an ally is too close, including a helping jungler. The malformed regeneration array is not used for an exact healing forecast.

item_notes.reason: Evade primes the slowing empowered basic attack, helping keep a spear trade in range. Fog-wall movement is conditional and the hit has its own cooldown.
Cast-attack weaving fits quick thrusts and Barricade releases. Haste does not allow empowered item hits more frequently than the item cooldown.
Repeated physical damage stacks armor reduction for the duel and team follow-up. Maximum stacks are earned through contact, not present on the first leap.
Physical armor and a nearby shred aura support remaining inside Coliseum. Allies still need a useful angle to attack the contained target.
Magical defense and a threshold cleanse can preserve the escape after entry. Flow State only resets on a takedown, so do not spend it assuming the kill.
Emergency health shielding and omnivamp support the committed arena trade. They do not make an isolated failed entry safe.

builds.review_scope: Cross-source role review: current role evidence, economy, six purchase reasons, kit delivery, selected loadout, counterplay and composition job. Conditional source build rates are not full-build win probabilities.
builds.rune_note: Authored for the stated kit and role. Blessings are checked against their Eternal and slot. Disputed blessing triggers are excluded from default plans; no whole-loadout win rate is inferred.
builds.title: Catch, survive, then repeat
builds.why: Use the quick Spear thrust for lane pressure and Barricade to absorb the response, then weave an attack after Evade. Coliseum is strongest when allies can hit the trapped target; Flow State resets movement only after a takedown, so plan an exit before committing.

builds.author: Codex editorial review
builds.caution: Infuse targets allies and is not an offensive on-hit spell. Vesh is selected for actual ability damage from Ricochet and Bad Medicine; the basic-attack DoT is not assumed to trigger every ability item. Avoid trading as though the offlane build were the support healing build.

item_notes.reason: Attack speed and magical on-hit damage support repeated Refibrillator attacks. The item’s on-hit effect is distinct from the native stacking DoT.
Ability damage stacks magical-armor reduction while health and omnivamp help trades. Refibrillator attacks alone do not establish the ability-triggered shred.
Earlier health contributes power, and magical damage can build Fiend over its interval. Simultaneous DoT ticks do not instantly grant all stacks.
Magical penetration helps damage against armor. Its additional effect specifically requires ability magical damage and the stated enemy-health condition.
Earlier spell shielding and magical defense protect positioning and a deliberate revival cast. The item does not extend Neural Regenesis’s revival window.
Late magical power supports the attack DoT, spells and revival health scaling. It comes after defense because dying outside the revival window defeats the plan.

builds.title: Control the approach and repeat the cast
builds.why: Use Refibrillator attacks between Bad Medicine and Ricochet casts, then step away while the damage-over-time effect runs. Disc of Demise rewards useful ricochets; it does not create extra damage by bouncing repeatedly onto the same target. Save Neural Regenesis for a credible lethal window.

builds.author: Codex editorial review
builds.caution: Triage Protocol and Lunaria require damage setup. Neural Regenesis must be active when lethal damage arrives; it is not a permanent second life. Rebirth’s physical power is an expensive automatic healer default, so this plan uses team protection instead.

item_notes.reason: Infuse can give the shared power/haste buff while mana regeneration supports the next heal.
Charge through safe damage, then spend the stored heal with Infuse.
The heal can help you and the recipient reposition.
Add short mitigation/Tenacity after the heal; this does not certify immunity to every control effect.
Damage applies anti-heal and healing can transfer it. It is a flex slot for the actual opposition.
Supports endangered allies and supplies conditional magic protection without buying physical power.
