- Orange Buff Omnivamp decreased from 8% to 5%.
On Saturday August 15th & Sunday August 16th, a 2-day Daybreak Invitational Tournament is happening. This will feature 8 Teams composed of the Top Players from NA PCC Summer!

This event will showcase the Daybreak Map in a more high-stakes environment, allowing us to gather deeper feedback on all things Daybreak as the best players from the North American Region put it through its paces!
For the Format, it is a Player Draft Event, meaning 8 Captains have been pre-selected from the Top NA PCC Summer Teams, who then draft the rest of their squad from the remaining PCC Player pool.
The Teams are competing for the grand prize of $1,000 and representation within the Daybreak Map when it fully releases, as well as additional Platinum Prizes of 50K & 25K for 2nd and 3rd place!

Finally, a Devs vs VennyVens (Reigning EU PCC Summer Champions) showmatch will be kicking off the event, so be sure to tune in to see if the VennyVens have what it takes to bring down the people’s champ, RGSACE!

- Saturday 15th August - [10am ET / 4pm CEST]: Dev Showmatch + Top 8 Swiss Bracket.
- Saturday 16th August - [10am ET / 4pm CEST]: Top 4 Double-Elimination Finals Bracket.

- Four New Eternals added.
- Reductions to the strength of Basic Attacks for the majority of Ranged Heroes at Level 1, thereby reducing the strength of Ranged Offlaners.
- Recalls are no longer interrupted by DoT Damage.
- Red/Blue Buff now drop a 2nd Buff on the Floor for the killing team after 20:00.
- Mini Prime now drops its Buff on the floor for the killing team, instead of granting the Buff to the Killer.
- Rivers/Blue/Cyan now grant Energy Regen on Kill.
- [Bugfix] Various Stacking Shred Effects now work correctly instead of capping out after the 1st instance of Shred.
- Hero Size now has a Max and Min Cap.
- Tower Platings no longer removed at 13:00.
- Tower Platings have been added to Tier 2 (Inner) Towers.
- Refillable Potions Heal less at Level 1.
- Ground Targeting Improved to be more accurate
- Heroes now display a team-colored Shadow beneath their location when in the air, making them easier to track.
- Enemy Fountain no longer 1-shots you, and instead deals ramping true damage the longer you stand inside of it.
- White Camps now despawn after 10s of being out of combat if the Camp Leader is killed.
- Respawned Inhibitors now have a Purple Material around them, better signposting they cannot attack you.
- Various Basic Attacks and Abilities should now no longer hit you/rubberband you back if you correctly Blink/Dash away from them (E.g: Boris Ultimate).
- Aim Assist Strength reduced slightly for Controller Users, but smoothened in other areas.
- Items now display a variety of new information and stats when hovered over on the Scoreboard.
- General outlier balance.
- And more!
- Aim Assist for Controllers has been adjusted to be slightly less sticky, while improving other areas of it that should make the gameplay experience smoother for Controller users.

Ever Blinked away from a Boris just to get grabbed by him despite your Blink cooldown being eaten? Or blinked away from a Crunch Uppercut just to get knocked up anyway? While this can still happen when accounting for higher Ping, these outcomes should happen FAR less, resulting in a smoother, and more skillful gameplay experience, as before Client-based prediction would overly-favour the Hero using the Ability to confirm a hit, rather than the Hero that successfully dodged it.

- Client-predicted Attacks such as Boris Ultimate or Basic Attacks will no longer hit you if you successfully Blink/Dash far enough out of their Range.
- In the case of certain dash abilities, (E.g: Boris Ultimate) when a successful dodge occurs, the attack will fail and now stop the attacking Hero at your previous location you blinked from.

Getting 1-shot by the Enemy Base is a little unintuitive and poorly signposted, while also just simply being less fun than having the chance to execute a celebratory dive when a match is about to end. Now, you can dive into the Enemy’s Fountain if you wish, and instead of being 1-shot, you will take heavy true damage that ramps up over time instead (most Heroes will die within 4-7s seconds at most, so it's not super easy to do).

- Enemy Fountain no longer 1-shots you.
- Now deals 50 (+4% Max Health) True Damage every 0.5s to you while in the zone. This damage increased by an additional 10 (+1.25% Max Health) Damage every tick, for a maximum of 130 (+14% Max Health) Damage each tick.
- Now Displays a Camera Lens Effect and plays an SFX when you enter the Enemy Fountain.

Ever been frustrated by accidentally firing a Ground Targeted Ability at a wall due to invisible collision?! Me too! With these changes, Ground Targeting will be more consistent and accurate to where you are actually aiming, resulting in additional precision and far less accidental mis-fires that were of no fault of the Player.

- Now Targets from the Camera, instead of the Hero Model, reducing the frequency of unintentional corner clipping when using Abilities such as Gideon’s Cosmic Rift.
- Now Targets from your Cursor correctly, instead of being slightly offset to the Left, making aiming more precise to the User’s actual intent.

Ever wondered how much damage your Combustion has dealt across a match? Or how useful a variety of other Items have been?! Well now you can tell by focusing the item on the Scoreboard. However, for this pass, not every Item could be covered just yet, but we are hoping to expand this functionality further in the future where possible!

- Various Items now display a range of statistics in-game, such as the damage they have dealt over the course of a match.
- You can view yours, or other Players’ Item stats, by hovering an Item on the Scoreboard.
- Stat tracking for other Items that were waived this pass (such as Tainted Items “Healing Reduced" and “Damage Blocked” by Shields) are on our list to do in a future update, as they are larger technical undertakings.
Heroes can now be more easily tracked when in the air (looking at you Wukong), as they now cast a clear shadow directly beneath them when they are in the air.

- Ally and Enemy Heroes now cast a shadowy decal beneath their location on the ground when they are in the air.
- Blue Shadow: Ally.
- Orange Shadow: Enemy.
- Inner Circle: Gets smaller the higher the Hero is in the air.

With the addition of various DoT effects into the game, such as Vesh’s Burn, we have decided to allow Recalls to go through even when affected by a DoT effect, as it is largely an obnoxious limitation that adds more frustration to gameplay than is necessary.

- Damage Over Time (DoT) Damage Effects no longer interrupt Recalls.
- Recall can now be cast immediately after taking damage, instead of having a 0.15s Cooldown.

Max/Min Size is being capped, helping resolve a variety of issues, including Camera issues on larger Heroes, and the strength of Heroes such as Tiny Titan Rampage who can become obnoxiously unfair to even try and hit when they are excessively small.

- Hero Max Size increase is now capped to 2.5x
- Hero Minimum Size Scale is now capped to 0.55x.

We are removing the ability to “dirty” a Jungle camp by leaving one alive, as this can lead to excessive snowball scenarios when abused in high level play, while being a generally unintuitive and unfun mechanic for the average player to engage with.
- Camps with multiple units (2/3/4/5 Camp) will now despawn after 10s of being out of combat if the Camp Leader is killed.

Blue and Red now drop an additional buff at 20-minutes when killed, meaning Junglers no longer have to forgo as much Gold and Experience when looking to hand off the Buff to an Ally Hero, and can still have one themselves! Oh, and it now grants Energy Regen, meaning it is valid for Energy Heroes to utilize!

- Now drops a second buff on the floor for 30s at the Buff’s original spawn location after 20:00 that can be picked up by a member of the killing team.
- The Red Buff Giant now changes color slightly after 20:00 to signify it will now drop an extra Buff.
- Blue Buff now also grants +5 Energy Regen.
A quick addition to Cyan Buff to ensure it has additional value for Energy Heroes like Scarlett.
- Now also grants the Killer 25% Max Energy Regen instantly.

Mini Prime now drops its buff on the floor at a fixed location when killed, meaning Junglers can now use their Hunt to secure the Buff without having to worry about how to hand it off to their Teammates. Be careful though, if you don't pick it up within 30s, it will disappear, meaning the Enemy Team has a chance to deny you even if you kill the Mini Prime!

- No longer grants its Buff to the Killer.
- Instead, upon dying, it now drops the Mini Prime Buff on the floor for 30s that can be picked up by a member of the killing team.
Like Blue Buff, Red Buff also drops an additional Buff at its spawn location when killed, post 20:00 game time!

- Now drops a second buff on the floor for 30s at the Buff’s original spawn location after 20:00 that can be picked up by a member of the killing team.
- The Red Buff Giant now changes color slightly after 20:00 to signify it will now drop an extra Buff.
A quick addition to River Buffs to ensure it has additional value for Energy Heroes like Scarlett.
- Now also grants the Killer +15 Energy Regen for 5s.
- Now also grants the Killer +25 Energy Regen for 5s.
Tower Platings no longer fall off at 13:00, meaning teams on the back foot still have a chance at claiming the standing gold and catching up, even when behind.

- Tower Platings no longer deactivate at 13:00, and now remain for the entire match.
- Tier 1 Plating Gold Reward decreased from 70 to 60.

Tier 2 Towers are also gaining Plates for the entire match, better allowing Tier 2 Pushes to result in some additional progress and gold gain, rather than it feeling like its not worth to even bother hitting a T2 Tower if you can't kill it in any single push (while also helping to slow down the rate that a single Split Push can destroy them, thanks to the Bonus Armors that Plates provide when destroyed).

- 4 Tower Platings added on each Tier 2 Tower. They remain for the entire match.
- Tier 2 Local Gold On Kill decreased from 400 to 250.
- Tier 2 Plating Gold Reward = 50.
The confusion around whether an Inhibitor is “fake” or not is now a problem of the past! Once an Inhibitor respawns, it will now be a different color, making it easier to spot at a glance.
- Respawned Inhibitors now display a Purple Material, better highlighting to Players that they cannot attack.

Cauterize is one of the least-used Blessings, and clogs up the Vermis Blessing set in such a way that it makes mix-ups in its 1st category way too restrictive for Ranged Users. As a result, we are removing it and replacing it with a new Blessing: Mechadrive.
Mechadrive is replacing Cauterize, offering a range of Heroes, from Twinblast to Boris, a new option to consider when running Vermis instead of being bound to Serration as hard.
- [New] Basic Attacks reduce your Secondary Ability’s Current Cooldown by 10% On-Hit. Reduced to 5% against Non-Heroes.

Marrow is receiving a soft rework, with it no longer allowing its User to heal off of Minions Waves. Now, Marrow’s Healing is loaded far more into Hero Combat, meaning its users cannot win the lane by default by simply taking a trade and healing off the Minion Wave. In return, AoE effects now heal for 65% Effectiveness, instead of the 33% Effectiveness imposed on Omnivamp, making the Eternal more useful to a range of Heroes in general, despite being a relatively similar strength in early-game skirmishes.
- [Soft-Rework] Heal for 6%/7%/8%/9% of damage dealt to Heroes, increased up to 15%/20%/25%/30% based on your Missing Health. (65% Effectiveness for AoE Attacks. 15% Effectiveness against Monsters).

Roses is receiving two changes: Firstly, it now has a cap on the amount of bonus gold it can offer, as previously it provided its Users with far too much Gold in snowball scenarios and led to absurd economic outcomes. Secondly, the previous Hero Kill Omnivamp Amplification Effect from Marrow is being granted to Roses, providing it some additional payoff now that the Gold has been limited.

- Bonus Takedown Gold is now capped at +100g (5 Takedowns).
- Hero Kills now also grant +50% Effectiveness of Marrow’s Major Blessing for 8s.
Ferocity is receiving another hit to the amount of Attack Speed it offers, in order to slow down the rate at which it ramps up and becomes oppressive when utilized by Ranged or DoT Heroes alike.

The King provides a significant amount of excess gold income, especially in various Range vs Melee matchups when it can be stacked relatively safely, and contributes too heavily to snowball scenarios. As a result, it is seeing a reduction.
- Gold on Basic Attack decreased from 7 to 6.
We’re undoing the previous nerf to Nihil, as it continues to be one of the weaker performing Eternals.
- Stat Effectiveness per Takedown or Level increased from 18% to 20%.

Feeding Frenzy provides a surprising amount of Attack Speed in a fight considering how little thought its Users must put into their position. We’re reducing its radius to ensure that Heroes must actually position with purpose and sit amongst a group of targets to get its full effect, rather than it incidentally tagging everyone in a fight with ease.

Immaculate continues to cause excessive stat-check scenarios, both in the early-game and in the late-game. Another reduction is required in the short-term to ensure laning dynamics and 1v1 interactions between Heroes are not warped as easily.

Masterpiece results in rather significant snowballing for the User’s that can leverage it reliably, such as Feng Mao, and Eden. A reduction is occurring to make a single kill less-overbearing to deal with in a fight.

Aion is another Gold generation Eternal that is providing too much value and warping the Economy curve of the average match too heavily - often resulting in lane performances being irrelevant when playing against it. Another reduction is occurring to make sure it is less universally useful, and more tailored to the Heroes that can reliably trigger it.
- Gold Gained From Ability Damage decreased from 7% to 6%.

Sacrifice is being reworked, as previously it was providing far too much free Mana Regen in the laning phase, allowing the likes of Shinbi and Argus to cheat the lane entirely with near-infinite Mana Pools simply from hitting the Wave. Now, Sacrifice User’s have to actually interact with their opponent and are rewarded by engaging in aggressive gameplay loops, preserving laning dynamics in a healthier manner.
- [Reworked] Damaging an Enemy Hero with an Ability grants 2.5% Missing Mana Regeneration over 5s. Hero Kills regenerate 20% Missing Mana over 5s.

With the previous round of changes to Akeron and him now possessing additional utility and damage from his Health Scalings, we’re looking to normalize his build options further by reducing the general strength of his Magical builds, as they are currently far overperforming his Tank or Physical alternatives.

- Magical Power Scaling decreased from 18% to 16%.
- Hero Missile Homing Radius decreased from 450u to 380u.

- Web Shot Magical Power Scaling decreased from 40% to 35%.
- Leap Magical Power Scaling decreased from 40% to 35%.
- Bite Magical Power Scaling decreased from 45% to 40%.

The previous round of changes to Argus were made to elevate the areas of his kit that were generally lacking, and to be in line with the other changes that happened to the majority of Mage’s across the class. With that now past us, we are reducing the general strength of his Particle Shredder, as well as heavily limiting the amount of free Mana he can restore throughout the lane by simply hitting Minions thanks to the changes to both his Augment and to Aion’s Sacrifice, better ensuring there is an appropriate Mana:Damage tradeoff when he’s looking to pump a target.

- No longer restores Mana when hitting Non-Heroes.
- Mana Restored when hitting Heroes increased from 10% to 12%.

- Damage decreased from 13/20/27/34/41 to 13/19/25/31/37.
- Magical Power Scaling decreased from 18% to 16%.
- Mana Cost changed from 12/14/16/18/20 to 13/14/15/16/17.
- Cooldown increased from 3 to 3.5.

Countess was one of the few Mages last patch that did not really receive a great benefit from the changes. For this pass, we’re pushing her late-game Ultimate Damage and Durability up slightly to bring her further up to speed, as the teamfighting stage of the game is where she starts to struggle to find windows for execution.

A quick bump to Crunch’s lesser used Augments, with Lunge Crunch returning to old values to better enable his Jungle play patterns, and Falcon Crunch offering some additional bang for its buck to better match the strength of the others.

- Empowered Right Crunch Damage increased from 15% to 20%.
- Empowered Right Crunch In-Air Cooldown decreased from +30% to +25%.

Dekker is the first Ranged Hero receiving a reduction to her base Physical Power, thereby reducing the strength of her early-game poking capabilities and creating a larger gap between the raw damage output of a Ranged Hero compared to a Melee Hero. The reason is largely the same for other Heroes with this style of change, so context will be skipped for other Heroes for the sake of time.

While it may not appear as much of a damage loss on the surface, the damage loss adds up over the course of a lane, and better enables Melee Heroes to posture into a Ranged Hero and close the distance. It should be noted that the changes are more heavy handed for Heroes that are more likely to appear in off-roles like Offlane, and in some cases the Physical Power loss is being returned through additional Growth to ensure that Carries especially still feel functional and with agency once the mid-game rolls around.

- Physical Power decreased from 60 to 57.
- Physical Power Growth increased from 3.6 to 3.8.

Alongside the Physical Power reductions described in Dekker’s Context section, Eden is receiving a shift to her Focal Lens Augment once again, as it can result in too much proportional Cooldown Reduction, and therefore too much Tachyon Lance spam in the late-game, especially when paired with items like Solaris. Instead of a flat reduction, it is now a percentage, normalizing the value to be far healthier in these cases.
- Tachyon Lance Cooldown Refund changed from 1s to 10% Total.

- Physical Power decreased from 53 to 49.
- Physical Power Growth increased from 3.8 to 4.
- Heat Generation Modifier decreased from 20%/35%/50%/65% to 12.5%/30%/47.5%/65%.

As a followup to the previous Feng Mao changes, we are now making some targeted changes to reduce the strength of Feng Mao at higher-ranks. The previous change helped normalize his clear and allow him to function a little more freely in the early-game, and now we’re looking to strip back some of this damage away from his Isolation Damage as it can result in too much abnormal burst and is best utilized by experience players. Likewise, his Ultimate Reset Timer is seeing a reduction, as in high-skill lobbies, a single reset results in too much pressure for too long of a period as it allows Feng Mao to skirt the outside of a fight with ample time to find the perfect window.

- Isolation Damage decreased from 25/36/47/58/69 to 25/35/45/55/65.
- Bonus Physical Power Scaling decreased from 30% to 25%.

Gadget is the first of a handful of cases where Shred Effects have not been functioning correctly, resulting in a significant loss in utility. This has been occurring since v1.14, and with it now resolves, we expect to see all affected Heroes and Items perform far better than before, and will be monitoring their performance moving forward.
Greystone was also affected by the Shred Bug, meaning he was only shredding Armor once, rather than 4 times. This has now been resolved.

Ikra is receiving a soft-rework to his Cascade Augment, as it continues to provide too much raw value with Items such as Oathkeeper, and is railroading his builds too hard to the point it has created a Balance Bottleneck due to how bound he is to those Items to succeed. Now that it no longer allows Brine to apply On-Hit effects, Ikra’s general strength can be better observed and tuned moving forward.

- No longer applies On-Hit Effects.
- [Reworked] Basic Attacks grant a stack. At 5 stacks, the next direct Brine hit deals 10 (+20% Magical Power) bonus damage. Ability hits grant Ikra 12% Attack Speed stacking up to 4 times (once per ability).
- Magical Power Scaling decreased from 50% to 45%.

Some Base Physical Power reduction for Iggy to diminish his strength further in the Offlane, in-line with the changes to other Ranged Heroes. And a quick bugfix that was resulting in him dealing an extra tick of damage with his Passive under specific circumstances.

- Physical Power decreased from 52 to 49.
- Physical Power Growth increased from 3.9 to 4.1.
- [Bugfix] Fixed an issue where Badlands Critter could deal double damage if Iggy Ignites a Target with a single stack on them.
Khaimera’s Unleash has suffered from a few bugs causing it to feel unresponsive and desynced. These have now been resolved.

- [Bugfix] Khaimera increased attack speed no longer liners after the effect ends.
- [Bugfix] Khaimera’s Basic Attacks should no longer feel desynced while Unleash is active or hitting a target after it has finished.

- Physical Power decreased from 21 to 20.
- Physical Power Growth increased from 1.6 to 1.65.

Alongside the general reductions to early game Physical Power, Morigesh’s Spirit Shred Augment was another case that was impacted by the Shred Bug causing only 1 instance of reduction to occur. This has now been resolved.

- Physical Power decreased from 52 to 50.
- Physical Power Growth increased from 3.8 to 4.

- Physical Power decreased from 58 to 55.
- Physical Power Growth increased from 3.8 to 4.

- Physical Power decreased from 54 to 52.
- Physical Power Growth increased from 3.4 to 3.55.
Narbash’s Percussive Tear was another instance of the Shred Bug occurring, and has now been resolved.
- [Bugfix] Fixed an issue where N3on could re-cast Final Thread while Rooted.

Alongside the general Physical Power reductions for Ranged Heroes, Phase is also receiving a large change to her Psychic Flare, with it no longer reducing her Blink Cooldown as Heavily. This will allow her opponents a far better chance at catching her out and locking her down in fights, especially in higher level play where this mechanic is utilized far more aggressively.
- Blink Cooldown On Hit increased from 1s to 2.5s.

Tiny Titan continues to stand out as Rampage’s premier Augment as it is seeing a reduction in the general shrink it provides. The reason for this is that Tiny Rampage affords him a form of pseudo-durability due to being so hard to hit, especially when paired with Krix and other Shrink effects, making him near impossible to deal with once he’s on top of a target. Combined with the Minimum Size Cap described above, Tiny Rampage should be a lot more manageable to strike down in a fight, and feel far more fair to fight against.
Some small but meaningful buffs for Riktor, aimed at increasing his general success in the Offlane and Jungle Roles now that he has been afforded some additional early game damage and clear speed.
- Damage per Level increased from 4 to 5.
- Pulse Damage Modifier increased from 50% to 75%.

Shinbi, much like Argus, benefits too heavily from engaging in passive gameplay loops that can be difficult for opponents to disrupt or interact with. In her case, she has historically been heavily tuned around a limited Mana Pool to ensure that she cannot sit back and farm passively with Line Tempo with too much ease, but with various new forms of Mana Sustain entering the game since the addition of Eternals, this is even less so the case. As a result, we are adjusting her Line Tempo to deal reduced damage to Minion waves after it hits a Minion, reducing the rate at which she can blast through Minion Waves at Level 5+. In return, Line Tempo itself is receiving a damage increase, making it stronger as a dueling tool that she can leverage in aggressive trades.

- Upon hitting a target, the Wolf now deals 60% damage to Minions that are hit afterwards.
- Damage increased from 70/105/140/175/210 to 85/125/165/205/245.
- Magical Power Scaling increased from 55% to 60%.

- Physical Power decreased from 57 to 54.
- Physical Power Growth increased from 2.4 to 2.55.

- Physical Power decreased from 61 to 57.
- Physical Power Growth increased from 3.4 to 3.6.
- Max Health Damage decreased from 0.3% to 0.25%.
- [Bugfix] Fixed an issue where Steel could Blink during his Ultimate.

Terra’s Axe Retrieval has been underutilized for a while now, with it not really providing enough raw value to justify its use. To open up some additional playstyles, it now grants her Highland Hurl some additional damage, thereby allowing Terra to consider a more axe-orientated playstyle.
- Now also grants Highland Hurl +15% Damage.

- Physical Power decreased from 57 to 55.
- Physical Power Growth increased from 3.2 to 3.35.

While TwinBlast is receiving the general Physical Power changes that are occurring to all Heroes, the previous hit to Solaris impacted his general strength so we are granting him back some Ability up-time to ensure he can keep up with the rest of the Carry Roster

- Physical Power decreased from 66 to 63.
- Physical Power Growth increased from 4.3 to 4.5.

- On-Hit Modifier increased from 150% to 170%.
- Cooldown changed from 12.5/11/9.5/8/6.5 to 13/11.25/9.5/8.25/6.

- Physical Power decreased from 60 to 57.
- Physical Power Growth increased from 3 to 3.2.

Offlane Zinx has been causing a stir as of late, with her general ability to both run down and escape opponents being too high. For this pass we are taking some more aggressive swings at her Offlane viability especially, with her now boasting a lot less poke damage and outright durability in the early-game, and a far longer window between Triage Protocol activations.
- Additional DoT Damage Dealt decreased from +50% to +35%.

- Health decreased from 685 to 670.
- Physical Power decreased from 50 to 46.
- Mana decreased from 340 to 320.
- Mana Regen increased from 1.75 to 2.
- BAT increased from 1.35 to 1.4.
- Cooldown increased from 17-4.25 (-1.75 per Level) to 24/17.5/11/4.5 at Levels 1/6/11/16.

With the reduction to Basic Attack Damage for many Heroes in the early-game, we can now more comfortably reduce the amount of free sustain provided by Potions in the early game, without having to fear excessive snowballing scenarios occurring as much by doing so.

With the addition of Satariel and its Demonic Bargain Blessing, we’re bumping up Lucky Feather’s Cost and Sell value by 50g to prevent players from purchasing it from match start as we deem that it would be an unhealthy strategy to allow.

- Cost increased from 700 to 750.
- Sell value increased from 400 to 450.
Ruthless Broadsword is another case of the Shred Bug occurring, essentially resulting in it, and both Viper and Basilisk respectively, Shredding no Armor. This has now been resolved.

Ashbringer was suffering from a bug that prevented certain multi-hit Basic Attack Damage from triggering its effect more than once per attack/burst, making it lose over half its value on certain Heroes. This has now been resolved.
- [Bugfix] Now correctly Triggers its Cooldown Refund Effect multiple times for Attacks such as Skyler’s Hypercharge, and multi-hit Basic Attacks such as TwinBlast and Lt. Belica.

Manta Scythe has seen a surge of play as of late, with it offering both a strong outlet of sustain, late-game scaling, and general burst potential. To ensure the Item does not cover too many bases, too strongly, we’re opting to drop its isolation damage once again, as this aspect of the Item’s effect can lead to excessive burst scenarios that go against the more sustained-fighting nature of the item.
- Divide & Conquer Isolation Damage decreased from +10% to +8%.
A quick hit to Omen’s Cooldown Refund, as currently it is contributing to excessive uptime for certain Ability Combos.
- Bestial Momentum Cooldown Refund decreased from 25% to 20%.

Augmentation has largely fallen out of favour in the recent months, with it struggling to keep up with other Items in its Class, especially since the adjustments to Physical Power across the Carry/Assassin/Fighter Classes in 1.14. Some additional Physical Power and a slight cost reduction is therefore being granted to bring its efficiency up to more relevant levels.

- Cost decreased from 3150 to 3100.
- Physical Power increased from 30 to 35.

Berserker’s Axe is another Fighter Item that doesn’t pull its weight in the damage department, and is struggling to serve its function as an aggressive roaming item for those that use it best. A small bump in its damage potential and sticking power are required to bring it back into contention.

- Physical Power increased from 40 to 45.
- Health decreased from 300 to 275.
- Blitz Slow decreased from 50% to 45%.
- Blitz Slow Duration increased from 0.75s to 1s.

Mutilator’s Basic Attack Effect is now having its damage extended to all Target Types, providing Junglers with an alternative choice alongside Manta Scythe and Sky Splitter for a sustain-focused 1st buy, as previously the lack of PvE damage made the Item feel like it had too high of an opportunity cost to consider.

- Mutilate now applies its Basic Attack Effect against Minions & Monsters.
- Mutilate Damage is capped at 20 against Minions & Monsters.

Rebirth continues to provide a little too much general value and uptime to its Users. Once again the effect is seeing a bump down in its general efficacy, alongside an increase to its cooldown to make it less universally present throughout a match.

- Cost increased from 2950 to 3000.
- Health decreased from 300 to 275.
- Mechanica Cooldown increased from 240 to 270.
- [Bugfix] Fixed an issue where it was possible to Blink during the Rebirth Resurrection state.
Magnify is the final Shred Effect that was affected by the aforementioned Shred Bug, making it only apply 1-stack of Shred. This has now been resolved.
Cursed Scroll continues to provide too much raw damage output when paired with Krix, and is seeing another reduction in its potency to bring it down to a healthier middle-ground.

- Curse Of Pain Damage decreased from 30 to 20.
- Forbidden Art Attack Speed decreased from 2.5% to 2%.

- Major Blessing: Additional Stats per Stack decreased from +12% to +10%.
- [Bugfix] Major Blessing: Now grants 2 stacks at Match Start as the Player starts the Match at Level 3.

- Major Blessing: Damage decreased from 1% to 0.75%.
- Major Blessing: Ability Haste decreased from 4 to 3.
- Major Blessing: Movement Speed decreased from 0.75% to 0.6%.
- Major Blessing: Max Health decreased from 1.5% to 1.2%.

- +3% Damage Dealt.
- -6% Damage Taken.
- +10 Ultimate Haste.
- Brawl now generally has the same gamemode specific balance changes to Heroes, Items and Eternals as ARAM.

- Passive Small Entity Drop Chance was 50% now 90%
- Passive Minute Threshold was 7 now 7.
- Passive Stacks Below Threshold were 8 now 10.
- Passive Stacks Above Threshold were 6 now 8.
- Passive Gains 1 Stack every 12s.

- Tiers stacks were 40/80/120/160 now 35/70/105/140
- Passive Gains 1 Stack every 10s

- Fixed an issue where, during Ranked Draft, on Dawn Team the second User could lose their Hero Selection upon the first user locking in their pick.
- Fixed an issue where Users could receive a placeholder Crest Screen if they had a removed Crest in their Loadout, such as Earth Spirit (RIP).
- Fixed an issue where Narbash’s Ultimate Mesmerize could trigger multiple Immobilize events, instead of just once.
- Fixed an issue where Users would be unable to change their Eternal if they had an invalid Augment selected.
- Fixed an issue where Green Buff’s Explosive Shield would not state its name in the Death Recap.
- Fixed an issue where the Gifting Button could flicker if hovered during Battlepass previews.
- Fixed an issue where a User’s selected Eternals could be swapped out to Default when swapping Roles in Draft.
- Fixed an issue where Changing Mode would display the ARAM pop-up, despite it being outdated.
- Fixed an issue where Controller Users were unable to navigate the Post-Match Scoreboard.
- Fixed an issue in Ranked Draft where, after picking a Hero to Ban, if the Ban does not go through, the Hero would still be highlighted and blank.
- Fixed an issue where AFK Players would be required to Vote during a Surrender Vote.
- Fixed an issue where Users would be unable to Basic Attack or Use Abilities if they Disconnect from a Match while using the Free-look function.
That’s it for this update! We can’t wait for you to get your hands on it - let us know what you’re most excited for on our Discord and Reddit!
Game Design and Community @ Omeda Studios

blocks: Everything you need to know about Balance Patch v1.14.4!

It’s balance time! Eternals totally shook up the meta since their arrival in 1.14, it’s been awesome to see how you’ve all been building and adapting with them.

This update is a larger balance pass to correct some issues we’ve seen with Eternals. We’re expecting a little more will be needed until we find that sweet spot though, so keep your feedback coming in!

We are introducing a new type of loot core in this patch called Bundle Cores. These cores will be available for limited time and contain a small collection of content, with no duplicate drops and every drop shares the same drop rate.
Premium Bundle Core - Contains 2 exclusive variants for Iron Guard Riktor and Deadzone Drongo plus a selection of previously available bundle exclusive variants from last year.
Victorious Bundle Core - Contains all victorious skins and a new Recall and Jumppad exclusive to this Bundle Core. Profits from this Core go directly to supporting Predecessor Competitive Events.

Thank you to everyone that shared feedback on the topic.

The PCC Summer Summit is here and will be kicking off with a 3-weekend event, starting on the 13th and 14th of June at 10 AM EDT/ 2PM UTC on the Predecessor Twitch channel. We'll also be co-streaming with some of your favourite content creators too!
Teams in EU and NA will be competing for a total prize pool of $14,000 and representation in Predecessor via 2d Cosmetics.
More info on the event here.
We will be running Twitch drops during the event weekends, as well as Platinum giveaways, so tune in to pick up some new content!
New OHE available from Twitch drops.

The prize pool and event costs for tournaments like this and other community events come from the profits made from the Victorious content. If you would like to support future events please consider picking up any of the Victorious skins, bundles and more!

We have introduced a Victorious Bundle Core to further support competitive events, which contains all Victorious Skins and a new Victorious Recall and Jumppad exclusive to the Bundle Core. Bundle Cores do not drop duplicate items.

Lastly it’s been requested for there to be more ways to donate towards Esports, so we are introducing a Luxury Donation Cosmetic. This Epic OHE is intended for those wishing to make a larger donation to PCC, so only consider purchasing this if you are willing to make that type of donation. 100% of the sales from this OHE will go into supporting Competitive events.

For this pass, we are primarily looking at smoothing out the gameplay experience and tidying up some of the balance/gameplay loop fallout that has occurred with the addition of the Eternals and the power they have provided. Specifically, this is being done by rounding out the rough edges for some of the more extreme balance outliers and Eternals that are causing extreme power spikes or offering too much/too little general value, with it hopefully resulting in a more well-rounded balance baseline. As we mentioned in the v1.14 update, our plan moving forward is to continue refining the balance ecosystem with the new Eternals in mind, which naturally will take a few more passes to get into a nice and stable spot, but for now this should be a positive step forward.

- Addition of some new Magical Power and Physical Power hybrid scalings to various Hero Abilities, opening up Eternal and Build diversity further.
- Tower Durability & Damage increased.
- Minion Durability increased.
- Hunt’s Slay Damage increased to 600/1200.
- Monster Durability increased slightly to compensate for the Hunt change.
- Various adjustments and reworks to Eternal Blessings to help address problem-cases, or make the lesser-picked options more viable in strength compared to the more popular options.
- Small increases to the base damage of various abilities (primarily Mages and Bruisers) to ensure their damage stays a little more relevant at the Level 3-9 thresholds as Durability spikes can result in the inability to adequately threaten kills at that range.
- General Hero Balance to bring the extreme outliers further into general parity.
- Buffs to some Fighter and Anti-tank Items.
- ARAM Tower Durability/Damage increases.
- And more!

- A range of Heroes (primarily Melee Fighters) are receiving the addition of some mixed scalings, such as Akeron regaining some of his lost Physical Power Scalings, or Zarus’ Spear Of Nyr now also scaling with Magical Power. 
- The intent of this change in the majority of cases is not to make the likes of Akeron build full Physical every match, or for Mage Zarus to be a viable option (trust me, it’s not), but rather to open up various hybrid Eternal options, such as Nihil, to a broader range of Heroes, or to further enable some alternative builds that are currently popular in the case of On-Hit Belica and Howitzer.
- Finally, this sets the groundwork for us to consider the addition of a few more Hybrid-power Items in the future now that more Heroes can utilize them.

We’re increasing the damage dealt by Hunt’s active effect to provide Junglers with a little more consistency when securing objectives, as currently there are a lot of chaotic moments where various Heroes with Percent Max Health mechanics can compete too closely for the last hit, leading to too much variation and potential for failure, even if the Jungler makes the correct play. As a result of this change, select Jungle Monsters are receiving a small increase to their Health to ensure that Junglers are not overly accelerated in their Clear Speeds thanks to the extra couple hundred damage they are capable of dealing.

- Slay damage increased from 500 to 600.
- Empowered Slay damage increased from 1000 to 1200.

For Cyan and Gold Buff, we are increasing their Durability once they hit Level 2-11 by a small amount, better allowing players to contest their opponent and interact around them, as currently it is a tad too easy to blow them up with little room for the opponent to respond at the 5-15 minute mark.

- Health adjusted from 1150-2550 (+100 per Level) to 1150/1350/1475…2475 (+125 per Level)
- Health now no longer scales past Level 11 (previously scaled up to Level 15.)

- Health adjusted from 1100-2500 (+100 per Level) to 1100/1300/1425…2425 (+125 per Level)
- Health now no longer scales past Level 11 (previously scaled up to Level 15.)
- Large Monster Health increased from 1550-2470 to 1650-2570.
- Large Monster Health increased from 1300-2220 to 1400-2320.

Tower Damage and Durability is seeing an increase as they were not appropriately scaled up to account for the increases to general Hero Base Durability and Damage that occurred in the v1.14 update. These changes should have Towers feeling more appropriately dangerous to dive, while better allowing them to hold up against a single push.

- Health increased from 5000 to 5800.
- Damage increased from 170-338 (+12 per Level) to 180-404 (+16 per Level).

- Health increased from 4000 to 5000.
- Damage increased from 185-423 (+17 per Level) to 200-522 (+23 per Level).

- Health increased from 3800 to 4500.
- Damage increased from 185-423 (+17 per Level) to 200-550 (+25 per Level).

Much like Towers, Minions also were not appropriately scaled to match the damage increases offered from the Eternals in v1.14. We will be making more adjustments to the dynamics of Minions in the near future to help refine the wave-clear and last-hitting experience more, but for now this increase to Health should help provide a longer window of interactivity in the mid-game onwards. Likewise, the last-hit Execute Threshold is increasing by a small amount to ensure that the proportional increase to Minion Health does not make low-damage Heroes such as Tanks suffer as heavily now that their relative Health is higher, and therefore, more difficult to farm correctly under Towers.

- Health increased from 750-1436 (+49 per Level) to 760-1558 (+57 per Level).
- Execute Threshold increased from 20% to 21%.

- Health increased from 435-897 (+33 per Level) to 450-982 (+38 per Level).
- Execute Threshold increased from 23% to 24%.

- Health increased from 1150-2950 (+100/200 per Level) to 1150-3260 (+115/240 per Level).
- Execute Threshold increased from 17% to 18%.

- Health increased from 1600-4820 (+230 per Level) to 1600-5240 (+260 per Level).
- Damage increased from 220-346 (+9 per Level) to 220-374 (+11 per Level).
- Damage dealt to Inhibitors Damage decreased from 50% to 40%.
- Damage dealt to Core decreased from 22% to 20%.
- Execute Threshold increased from 17% to 18%.
- [Bugfix] Fixed an issue where Vermis’ Damage could trigger Spellshield effects.

Serration: 
Serration is seeing a rework, with it no longer requiring a Critical Chance build to increase the damage of the Main Vermis effect, and instead being a more consistent value On-Hit that more Heroes can benefit from.
- [Reworked] Vermis deals an additional 4% Target’s Missing Health Damage on activation.

Cauterize: 
Cauterize is seeing its effect expanded with a soft rework. As there are not many DoT damage sources present across Heroes, its effect of offering Health Regen while affected by a DoT was too niche. We have now expanded this to any source of Ability Damage (and Passive, such as Morigesh’s Pestilence) to better allow it to serve as an Anti-poke option against a wider range of opponents for Vermis users that need some extra in-lane survivability.
- [Soft-rework] Cauterize: Taking Ability or Passive Ability Damage grants you 2 (+0.5 per Level) Health Regen for 2s.

Breach: 
A small increase in Duration for Breach’s Shred, better allowing its users to capitalize on the Shred once their Ultimate has finished casting.

Sub Surface:
Sub Surface is currently offering a deceptively strong amount of Damage Reduction. As the majority of the Abilities in Predecessor are AoE, this is effectively a 10% durability increase to Ability Damage, and therefore needs a reduction to ensure it does not make squishier users overly durable, considering the amount of damage Vermis users are capable of.
- AoE Damage Reduction decreased from 10% to 8%.

The Maw: 
Much like Vermis’ Serration, The Maw is also seeing a soft rework to move it away from requiring a Critical Strike build to see value. Instead, it is now simply a less potent damage amp against low-health targets, opening it up to more users. Finally, we have flipped it from Category 1 to 2 in order to encourage more direct opportunity cost and builds within the Marrow Tree, based on playstyle.

- [Soft Rework] Basic Attacks deal an additional 12% True Damage to targets below 30% Max Health. 
- Moved to Category 2, swapped with Leech.

Blood Bank: 
Blood Bank is currently offering too much Lifesteal, able to reach levels of 30%+ with relative ease in end-game scenarios. This is too much in combination with Marrow’s Major Effect, and in need of a reduction.
- Lifesteal per 100 charges decreased from 1% to 0.75%.

Leech: 
Leech is another Minor Blessing that feels a bit too niche and weak relative to other Minor Blessings in the system. To help solidify it as a more potent early-game option, we have increased the amount of Regeneration it steals by 2x, making it great for Melee Heroes that like to engage in drawn out, close-range engagements. And for those sharp-eyed readers that are questioning how you can steal more than 100% of the Enemy’s Base Regeneration? The way it works is you gain 200% of whatever Base Health Regen value the Enemy has, meaning they are set to 0. The remaining 100% is dealt to them as a true damage aura that will damage them for that value every second.

- [Soft Rework] Base Health Regeneration Steal increased from 100% to 200%
- Effect Radius increased from 400u to 550u. 
- Moved to Category 1, swapped with The Maw.

Golden Mane:
Golden Mane felt a little too specialized when it was only effective against single-target abilities, as there are not too many of them across the Hero Kits. To make it more versatile against a wider range of opponents, we are now extending its Damage Reduction to Basic Attacks, but reducing the potency of the effect to compensate for its more general application.

- Damage Reduction decreased from 12% to 8%.
- Now grants 8% Damage Reduction against all Non-AoE Attacks.

Rallying Roar:
Rallying Roar struggle to compete with the other options in its category, and is receiving some additional Ultimate Haste to not only lean further into a Thraex Ultimate Build archetype, but to also ensure it competes more effectively with Ferocity, and the now improved Golden Mane.

Growing Threat: 
Growing Threat is receiving a small but meaningful adjustment, with it losing some damage but now offering an avenue of sustain to Nihil users. This better shapes it towards the Bruisers that benefit from Nihil’s Major Blessing the most, reducing the general burst they are capable of, but offering a small but meaningful way to accrue some additional sustain that will help them stay in the fight as their Nihil effect ramps up in the later stages of a match.

- Bonus Damage decreased from 15% to 12%.
- Now also grants 5% Omnivamp at 18 Minutes.

From The Abyss: 
From The Abyss is one of several sustain-based Minor Blessings that are seeing a reduction in this pass. As it stands, they are all granting too much sustain in the laning phase, allowing their users too much freedom to take poor trades and ignore wave-states. This shuts down too much laning interaction too quickly, and so we have opted to make it scale as a match progresses. This change makes it a meaningful source of durability in the late-game, but ensures laners still have to employ skill throughout the laning phase in order to survive and achieve leads.
- Max Health Regen changed from 0.4% to 0.2/0.4/0.7/1% at Levels 1/6/11/16.

Major Blessing:
Krix is currently offering too much durability throughout a match, especially in the early lane where raw Health is the most valuable form of defense. This has led to many seemingly unkillable Melee Heroes arising in the laning phase while also benefitting its users with high-damage output for health-scaling abilities/item effects, and is in need of a reduction.
- Max Health decreased from 10% (+1% per Level) to 5% (+1% per Level).

Voracity:
Similar to many of the other sustain-based Eternals, Voracity is simply granting too much in-lane sustain currently. This leads to many Krix users being overly difficult to pressure and punish in the lane, leading to stagnant lanes too quickly into a match. However, the reduction is being offset with a small Gold Gain effect, better differentiating it from Regenerative Tissue as an early-game acceleration option to help weaker Tanks progress to item breakpoints faster, whereas Regenerative Tissue will be more valuable in the late-game as a general purpose sustain option.

- Max Health Healing on Unit Kill decreased from 1.25% to 1%. 
- Now also grants +2 Gold on Unit Kill.

Regenerative Tissue: 
Regenerative Tissue currently makes poke damage too easy to shake off, and is seeing a change that reduces its strength in the early lane especially, while becoming more powerful in the later stages of a match as this is where Tanks start to fall off relative to damage dealers.
- Max Health Regeneration changed from 0.4% to 0.2%/0.4%/0.8%/1.2% at 1/6/11/16.

Cannibalism: 
With the amount of Health being offered by Krix being reduced, we’re granting Cannibalism a small increase to ensure it remains relevant as a form of scaling durability for its users.
- Health on Takedown increased from 30 to 35.

Mending:
Mending is another sustain-based blessing that is resulting in lane-phase stagnation, providing its users with simply too much regeneration that negates poke damage too heavily. It now scales with Level, ensuring it is still powerful in the late stages of a match, but less forgiving in the early stages of a lane.
- Missing Health Regeneration changed from 6% to 4%/5%/6%/8% at Level 1/6/11/16.

Phylactery 
Phylactery is seeing a small soft rework aimed at opening it up to more Users, shifting some of its strength away from its Shielding effect that only Gideon really benefits from, and now granting some additional cooldown progression as well. This is a great choice for any Hero looking to benefit from a momentum reset mid-fight, as it speeds up how quickly the Users cooldowns regenerate by a whole 3s faster after you use your Ultimate, granting faster access to a second rotation of Basic Abilities.

- [Soft Rework] Casting your Ultimate now also grants to 100% Cooldown Progression for 3s
- Shield Max Mana Scaling decreased from 20% to 15%.
- Shield Duration decreased from 4s to 3s.

Xyris currently underperforms too heavily compared to other Eternals, primarily due to how slow and backloaded its Damage effect is. To help smooth out its power curve, we’re granting it some upfront Damage, in return for less overall late-game scaling post-30m.
- Damage Amplification changed from 0% (+0.75% per 10 units killed) to 4% + (0.6% per 10 units killed).

Cull The Weak: 
Cull The Weak now grants a small amount of Mana Regen to its users, helping open up Xyris as an alternative Eternal choice for Heroes such as Argus and Kwang that want to benefit from the Xyris’s Damage effect, but often feel constrained by their Mana Economy which they can now overcome. And with Xyris gaining some base damage, we’re also reducing the Damage from Cull The Weak to ensure it is not too mandatory for Junglers or contributing to excessively fast clears.

- Minion & Monster Damage decreased from 10% to 8%.
- Now also restores 1% of Missing Mana on Unit Kill.

Furor: 
Furor, while powerful in its own right, drops off a touch too quickly considering it is only accessible once per fight - especially in reactive scenarios. We’re granting it some additional duration to better allow its users to keep up the onslaught of attacks when they commit or react to an engagement.
- Attack Speed Duration increased from 4s to 4.5s.

Dominance: 
Dominance tends to lack impact in the early game due to the majority of its Healing being loaded into its Missing Health Component, which struggles to feel meaningful in the early game. To ensure it can compete with the other buffed Xyris options, we’re bumping up the base to allow it more opportunity to enable its users to turn the tides in early game engagements.
- Healing on Takedown increased from 50 to 100.

Iron Will: 
As with the changes to Vermis’ Serration, and Marrow’s The Maw, Iron Will is also seeing a shift away from being purely Critical Strike driven to make it more versatile, with it now granting some generic consistency that will be applicable to various Carries throughout the lane, regardless of whether they opt for an On-Hit or Critical Strike build.
- [Soft Rework] Basic Attacks now also heal you for 3% of damage dealt, increased to 8% for Critical Strike Basics.

Bone Collector: 
Bone Collector was not really offering any intrigue in its offering, with it simply being just another unreliable, back-loaded damage amp with its offering of additional power on takedown. Now that we have adjusted other Xyris Blessings, we are adjusting Bone Collector to offer its users a unique source of Critical Strike Chance in the mid-late game, allowing for new build possibilities offering a far more compelling mid to late game benefit that is worth the trade off of the slower start.
- [Reworked] Upon Killing 150 Units, gain 20% Critical Strike Chance and 5% Critical Damage.

Eviscerate: 
A small but meaningful reduction in the damage threshold of Eviscerate in exchange for less raw burst, making its damage amp a little more accessible and consistent against targets that linger around these higher health thresholds.

- Damage Decreased from 20% to 15%.
- Health Threshold decreased from 85% to 80%.
- [Bugfix] Fixed an issue where Exarch’s Damage would not trigger on On-Hit Abilities.

Lotus is currently offering too much potency through its potential offering of durability and damage, with each being too potent in isolation, and the combination of high damage and durability making too many damage classes too well-rounded in stat profile. A reduction in both is needed to ensure the power of Lotus is more in line with other Eternals, while ensuring it is still accessible and meaningful to a wide range of users.

- Bonus Damage decreased from 1.75% to 1.5%.
- Bonus Max Health decreased from 2% to 1.5%.

Early Bloom:
Early Bloom results in a very powerful Experience spike when the user reaches level 10, as it effectively grants access to a Hero’s Rank 2 Ultimate a level early. This spike happens rather early into a match, and can feel very oppressive to play into. To help remedy this and push the Blessing more into mid-game strength territory, we are shifting the required Level Threshold back to 12, helping to avoid the Level 11 spike, while being a low enough level that the base stat increases and time saved from it are not equally as oppressive compared to offering at a higher level such as 14.
- Level Up Threshold increased from Level 10 to 12.

Immaculate:
Immaculate currently offers far too much durability to various Shield users such as Riktor that can maintain the threshold. Likewise, it is being taken to offer raw boxing potential in the midlane, with its users overly empowered to take level 1 trades that the opponent cannot match. As a result we are significantly lowering the Damage Reduction provided to ensure that the initial trade received is more potent and equal, but reducing the Threshold so that it is more generically available.

- Damage Reduction increased from 35% to 20%.
- Health Threshold decreased from 90% to 85%.

Fragrance:
Fragrance was too niche in its effect due to the limited number of True Damage sources across the Hero Abilities, primarily being an Adele-only choice. To help open it up and offer Magical Heroes another option, we are shifting its effect to also amplify Magical Damage at a smaller ratio, better suiting it to the likes of Kwang and Countess that like to get into the fight, while also offering a less risky option to Prima Donna for Mages in general.

- [Soft Rework] Now also amplifies a Hero’s Magical Damage by 5% against nearby Enemy Heroes, instead of just True Damage.
- Bonus True Damage decreased from 15% to 12%.

Bloatware:
Bloatware currently exists in a problematic space that is offering the incredible combination of damage and durability to a range of high-damage threats, resulting in heavy stat-check gameplay where Carries hit like a truck but cannot be killed in the late-game. To ensure that there is a greater tradeoff in damage potential to the durability offered, especially relative to other Eternals, we are reducing the Damage Amp portion of the effect.

- Damage Amplification decreased from 1% to 0.5%.
- Moved to Category 2, swapping with Construct.

Construct:
Construct is another Blessing offering too powerful of a mix of durability and damage to damage-based classes, resulting in a similar issue of high-damage threats being too durable for many Bruisers, Mages, and Tanks to burst through. It is receiving a rework to shift it to a mixed Health+Ability Haste option, ensuring that the Demiurge Tree remains accessible to Bruisers, Mages and Tanks alike, but reducing the raw durability and damage offered across the whole tree when it is taken in combination with Bloatware.

- [Reworked] Now grants +10 Health, +1.25 Ability Haste per Level.
- Icon changed from Physical Power to Ability Haste.
- Moved to Category 1, swapping with Bloatware.

Bottomless Vial: 
Bottomless Vial’s reward is a little too low for how unreliable its condition is. We’re granting it a small boost to make it more attractive to midlaners that want a larger power boost from Category 1.
- Magical Power on River Buff Kill increased from 4 to 5.

Perfection:
Given the lack of durability present in Aion’s Blessings, it can be rather difficult for Perfection's HEalth threshold to be maintained, making it overly conditional. To bring some additional consistency, we’re extending the Threshold.

Runic Focus:
As Aion is more centered around acceleration in its User's build thanks to its gold gain effect, there are many cases where the effects fall off too heavily in the late-game relative to other Eternals thanks to the damage foregone. To bring some additional late-game damage insurance for Mages, a bump to Runic Focus’ Magical Power amp is being offered.
- Magical Power based on Current Mana increased from 0.15% to 0.2%.

- Various Heroes are receiving the addition of new Mixed Scalings to their Abilities, opening up Eternal and Item diversity slightly further.
- Various Mage and Bruiser Heroes are receiving small Base Damage increases (+5/+10 or so) to ensure their abilities deal an appropriate amount of damage relative to their mana costs during the laning phase as base durability from levelling up starts to ramp up.

Adele is currently overperforming in the Support role, offering too much versatility thanks to her mix of lower cooldowns, innate durability, and high incidental damage potential. We’re trimming down some of this strength, making her a little more manageable to lane against, especially in the early game where she thrives the most.

Tyrant Of Thorns [Augment]:
- Bonus Movement Speed decreased from 55% to 50%.

General:
- Health decreased from 690 to 685.
- Physical Armor decreased from 38 to 36.

Crown Of Thorns [Passive]:
- True Damage decreased from 8% to 7%.

Royal Flourish [Primary]:
- Cooldown increased from 12s to 13s.
- Bonus Movement Speed decreased from 40% to 25%.

Rejoice Physical Akeron enjoyers! We have returned some of his lost Physical Power Scalings after receiving a wide range of feedback from Akeron mains that enjoyed his old scaling structure. This re-enables him to take a more hybrid approach with his build, once again allowing him to benefit from Items such as Earthshaker, Draconum, or Basilisk, should he desire.

Web Lash [Secondary]:
- Leap Damage decreased from 70/95/120/145/170 to 60/85/110/135/160.
- Slam Damage now also Scales with 50% Bonus Physical Power.

Crushing Maw [Alternate]:
- Magical Power Scaling increased from 40% to 45%.
- Damage now also Scales with 75% Bonus Physical Power.

Consume [Ultimate]:

- [Bugfix] Fixed an issue where Viper was not Shredding Armor correctly.
A quick bump for the Penetration offered by Deathstalker, making it a more attractive pickup earlier in Penetration-heavy builds.

To help combat the efficacy of Tanks, we’re increasing the base damage of Infernum’s Cinder effect to ensure it feels like a meaningful counter-buy when picked up earlier in a match as a response to a tankier enemy composition.
- Cinder Max Health Damage increased from 3% to 4%.

Nightfall is receiving some additional Omnivamp to bolster its ability to serve as an alternative to Mutilator for Assassins in need of sustain when fighting bulkier targets in the Offlane, as currently it typically can only be picked up in the latter half of builds.

Augmentation has heavily fallen out of favour, often being overlooked for other alternatives even by its core users such as Crunch. A bump to its True Strike damage and Ability Haste is being offered to cement it as an appropriately desirable first-buy for the Heroes that utilize it best.

- Ability Haste increased from 16 to 20.
- True Strike Base Physical Power Scaling increased from 80% to 90%.
- Corrode Physical Armor Shred increased from 4% to 4.5%.

With the increase to damage stats for various Carry and Assassin Items in v1.14, Mutilator has been left behind considering it straddles the line of desirability for Bruisers and Assassins alike. To ensure it has adequate useability, it is receiving an increase to its damage in line with other options, as well as some additional Omnivamp to better serve as a response that allows more aggressive repeat trades against tanky opponents.

- Physical Power increased from 40 to 45.
- Omnivamp increased from 10% to 12%.

Solstice currently offers too much upfront burst potential from a single attack in end-game scenarios. A reduction to this late-game potential is needed to ensure Heroes such as Feng Mao do not have the capability to 1-shot an opponent late-game as freely.
- Mornfall Physical Power Scaling decreased from 0-60% to 0-55%.

Carapace is another Fighter item that was left behind in the stat transition of v1.14, feeling like it offers too little durability to be useful to Bruisers, and too little damage to be competitive with other options for Duelists and Assassins. A small bump in both departments is being offered to allow it to better function as an aggressive early-game choice when more specialized options are not required.

- Physical Power increased from 40 to 45
- Health increased from 200 to 225.

With the addition of various Eternals that offers Mages innate Health scaling, and the general slow-down and high-sustain of many matchups that result in low-punishment scenarios, Orb Of Growth is currently offering too much Mana, which allows too much economic forgiveness for standard Mages to sit on without meaningful tradeoffs. A reduction in Mana is occurring to ensure that the bulk and scaling Orb offers comes with a more limited Mana Pool that the enemy can attempt to run dry compared to heavier Mana-based Items.

Alongside the Mana reduction, Orb Of Enlightenment is seeing a reduction to the Magical Power it offers, as currently the damage tradeoff for the durability it provides when paired with various Eternal effects is not distinct enough, contributing to an over-representation of Magical Bruiser builds in the mid-lane.

- Mana decreased from 300 to 250.
- Enlightened Magical Power per Level decreased from 4 to 3.

Cursed Scroll’s effectiveness has heavily benefitted from the increase to Base Health and Health-based Eternal effects, resulting in some rather excessive damage output and regeneration. A drop in both is needed to correct this.

- Curse Of Pain Health Scaling decreased from 5% to 4%.
- Forbidden Art Base Health Regen decreased from 30% to 25%.
- [Bugfix] Fixed an issue where Curse Of Pain would trigger on Cleave Damage, which could result in the User taking excessive damage.

Similar to the main mode, Towers in ARAM have not been adequately adjusted in line with the new damage and durability that many Heroes possess. To resolve this, we’re increasing both aspects for the Inner Tower and Inhibitors, ensuring that the progression of Towers falling in ARAM is more consistent and that games end in less sudden ways.

Inner Tower:
- Inner Tower Health increased from 9000 to 10800.
- Inner Tower Damage increased from 180-390 (+15 per Level) to 180-530 (+25 per Level).

Inhibitor:
- Inhibitor Health increased from 6500 to 8000.
- Inhibitor Damage increased from 180-390 (+15 per Level) to 180-530 (+25 per Level).
With Nitro returning, we have made some quick Nitro-specific Balance adjustments for the Eternals to ensure that they are appropriately tuned to the faster environment.

Nihil:
- Growing Threat: Time to activate decreased from 18 Minutes to 11 minutes.

Krix:
- Voracity: Maximum Health Healing increased from 1% to 1.75%.

Vesh:
- Vesh: Damage per Minute increased from 0.5% to 0.75%.
- Milennia: Ultimate Damage per Minute increased from 1% to 1.5%.

Aion:
- Philosopher: Gold Gained per Interval increased from 5 to 12.
- Bottomless Vial: Permanent Magical Power per River Buff Kill increased from 4 to 7.

- Fixed an issue where Users could get stuck in an Infinite Loading Screen upon loading into a match.
- Fixed an issue with Replays where Hero Healthbars could become hidden if the User skipped time.
- Fixed an issue where Controller Users could have their Movement Inverted if they set their deadzone above 40% while playing on the Alternative Layout.
- Fixed an issue where Serath could become temporarily stuck inside an Enemy Hero if she uses Heaven’s Fury on a Hero that enters Stasis.
- Fixed an issue where Legion’s Basic Attack Description did not state it scaled Physical Power in the Main Menu.
- Fixed an issue where Legion’s Press The Advantage Augment Description would not show its Attack Speed increase in the Main Menu.
- Fixed an issue where Legion’s Lord Commander Skin could show a duplicated Grenade on his waist.
- Fixed an issue where Riktor would not play his Spawn VO correctly with various skins.
- Fixed an issue where Alternator’s Stack count would visually go above its cap on the User’s HUD.
- Fixed an issue where Controller Users would be unable to focus the Eternal for a Build Loadout in the Guide View Tab.
- Fixed an issue where Yin was classed incorrectly as Frontline in the Collection Menu.
- Fixed an issue where Phase’s Support Recommended Items did not include a Divine Potion.
- Fixed an issue where Idrisil's Shield effect could trigger at a lower health value than intended.
- Fixed an issue where Wraith's Sonar Drone would not reveal Enemy Wards upon reaching Level 6.
- Fixed an issue where opening the Scoreboard during a Replay would display the incorrect upper Team UI elements.
That's everything for this Balance Patch! Thanks for reading, and we'll see you on June 9th when the update goes live.

Rei & Steggs
Game Design & Community @ Omeda Studios

From the world of Aresium comes the highly decorated shock trooper, Legion. A fanatical hand of an empire dedicated to bringing the galaxy under a single, united rule. Produced for absolute loyalty and peak efficiency, he has survived countless battles as a disciplined instrument of the Aresium Empire, a force that seeks to "liberate" the stars from the chaos of tyrannical freedom.

For generations, his batch-engineered brothers have served as a righteous hand of order, mastering the arts of battlefield logistics and ballistic weaponry to crush any who would oppose their mandate. As a total believer in the cause, Legion revels in the destruction of his enemies, finding his greatest joy in fighting and dying for the glorious empire that gave him life.

Legion’s newest mission has seen him deployed as a heavy-weapons anchor to far-flung battlefields, tasked with enforcing imperial doctrine by any means necessary. He descends upon the front line not as a mere soldier, but as a siege engine of order, stopping at nothing to ensure total purification and the expansion of the Empire’s reach.

Eternals are powerful deities in the Predecessor universe, capable of granting meta-defining “blessings” to worthy Heroes who choose to follow them.

This is a massive new gameplay system that redefines Hero customisation in the game, enabling you to pick from a huge range of Blessings for any Hero you want. Blessings range from high-risk berserker types, who thrive under near-death situations with extreme lifesteal, to unbreakable tanks who scale Max HP infinitely, and everything in between!

Eternals are a new gameplay customization feature, replacing the Minor Augments. Eternals allow Players to select one of twelve Deities during the Draft Phase of a Match, based on their gameplay preferences.
Each Deity offers the Player that selects them a powerful unique Major Blessing which is a Passive Effect that persists throughout a match.
Additionally, after choosing an Eternal, Players can choose 2 additional Minor Blessings from 2 sets of 3 Minor Blessings that are unique to that specific Eternal.

Eternal Blessings, like Augments, are active from Match start and, once selected for the first time, will be remembered across matches on a per Hero, per role basis, unless you change them. This means if you pick Eternals for Argus in Midlane, and want to play him again in your next match in the same role, the system will remember. If you take him into Support instead, it will go back to the recommended until you change your Eternals for Argus in Support.
In simpler terms, you now start the match with:

- 1 Hero Augment.
- 1 Eternal Major Blessing.
- 2 Eternal Minor Blessings.

All 12 Eternals will be unlocked when a player reaches level 10. Players that have not yet reached Level 10 will automatically be given pre-determined Eternals, and respective Minor Blessings, based on their Hero/Role chosen.
Eternals are thematically grouped based on gameplay archetypes and lore. However, these groupings are not prescriptive for gameplay, so we encourage Players to experiment with the Eternals.

In other words, this means that you do not necessarily need to take a “Carry Eternal” while playing as a Carry in order to find success, and could try a “Fighter” or “Supportive” Eternal instead if they synergize well with your Hero or Build!

Description: Cataclysmic entities of finality, existing solely to unravel the tapestry of creation with cold, relentless efficiency

Harbingers are best suited to Heroes looking to increase their combat capabilities through sustained attacks and drawn out combat engagements.
- Every 3rd consecutive Basic Attack against the same Enemy Hero within 2.5s, deals 3% (+0.25% per Level) of their Max Health as bonus Physical Damage.

- Serration: Vermis’ Major Blessing is 65% more effective on Basic Attacks that Critically Strike.
- Crush: When you Immobilize an Enemy Hero, deal 5% of their Maximum Health as bonus Physical Damage.
- Cauterize: When damaged by a DoT, gain 2 (+0.5 per level) Health Regeneration for 1s.

- Melting Point: Deal 10% bonus Damage to targets with more than 125 Physical Armor.
- Breach: Damaging an Enemy Hero with your Ultimate Ability decreases their Physical Armor by 30% for 3s.
- Sub-Surface: Take 10% less damage from AoE Abilities.
- Gain 0.5% (+0.05% per level) Omnivamp per 5% Missing Health. This bonus doubles for 8s upon killing an Enemy Hero.

- The Maw: Critical Strikes deal an additional 20% Bonus True Damage to targets below 25% maximum health.
- Blood Bank: Gain 100% of damage dealt to Heroes as charges for 3s. Gain 1% Lifesteal per 100 charges.
- Taste of Iron: Damaging an Enemy Hero with a DoT increases your damage dealt by 6% for 3s.

- Roses: Achieving a Takedown grants 20 Bonus Gold per previous Takedown.
- Jealousy: Deal 10% bonus damage against Enemy Heroes with more current health than you.
- Leech: Enemy Heroes within 400 units have their base Health Regeneration decreased by 100%, granting it to yourself.

Description: Domineering entities known for their raw strength and unquenchable thirst for conquest, standing alone as the supreme arbiters of war.

Primarchs are best suited to Heroes looking to dive into the fray of battle, offering a healthy mix of durability and damage.
- Mark the last Enemy Hero damaged by your Basic Attack for 3s, increasing your damage against them by 3% (+0.5% per level) and decreasing damage taken by them by 1.5% (+0.4% per level).

- Alpha's Court: Deal 6% Bonus Damage when there is no Allied hero within 800 units.
- Savage Strikes: Deal 1.5 (+0.4 per Level) physical damage On-Hit, increasing by 100% for 3s when you attack an Enemy Hero, stacking up to 3 times. Heal equal to the damage dealt.
- The King: Basic Attacks against Enemy Heroes grant you 7 gold.

- Ferocity: Gain 2% Total Attack Speed for every 1s spent in Hero Combat, stacking infinitely. Stacks are lost upon exiting Hero Combat.
- Rallying Roar: Upon casting your ultimate, yourself and Allied Units within 1500 units gain 20% movement speed for 4s.
- Golden Mane: Take 12% less damage from non-AoE abilities.

- Damage a Hero to gain Doom for 3s. Doom grants 1 Physical Power, 2 Magical Power, 1 Physical Armor & 1 Magical Armor for every 3s it persists. Upon levelling up, or achieving a Takedown, the stats offered by Doom are permanently increased by 20%.

- Growing Threat: At 18 minutes, gain +15% Bonus Damage permanently.
- From the Abyss: Restore 0.6% of your Maximum Health per second while in Hero Combat or standing out of Enemy Vision.
- Mana Siphon: Every time you hit an Enemy Hero with an Ability, steal 10 (+1% Target's Maximum Mana) Mana from them.

- Adaptive Plating: Taking Physical Damage grants 1% Physical Armor (Stacks 8 times). Taking Magical Damage grants 1% Magical Armor (Stacks 8 times). Stacks reset out of Hero Combat.
- Inescapable: Enemy Heroes within 800u that dash, leap or blink are Slowed by 20% for 1.5s.
- Terror: Minions and Monsters deal 30% less damage to you. Towers deal 15% less instead.

Description: Enduring entities known for their boundless resilience and absolute power, standing against the stars as immovable forces of nature.

Dreadnoughts are best suited to Heroes looking to increase their durability, disruption capabilities, better allowing them to thrive in the thick of combat.

- Voracity: Upon Killing an Enemy Unit, restore for 1.25% of your Maximum Health.
- Regenerative Tissue: If you haven't taken damage from a Hero for 8s, regenerate 0.6% Maximum Health per second.
- Festering Wounds: Enemy Heroes damaged by your DoT ability effects receive 45% less Healing for 2s.

- Cannibalism: Takedowns permanently increases your Maximum Health by 30.
- Feeding Frenzy: Gain +12% Attack Speed for every Enemy Hero within 1500 units.
- Predator: Camp Leader kills grant 8% Bonus Damage for 20s. Duration is 2x longer for Epic Monsters kills.

- Idrisil: While off cooldown and above 30% Max Health, gain 15% increased Physical and Magical Armor. Falling below 30% Health consumes this bonus, granting a 4s Shield equal to 150% of your total Armors. (CD: 75-32.5s)

- Cold Hearted: Enemy Heroes that basic attack you have their movement speed decreased by 2% for 2s, stacking up to 5 times.
- Mending: After taking damage from an Enemy Hero, restore 8% of your missing health over 3s.
- Frost Snap: Deal 10% Bonus Damage to Immobilized Targets.

- Icy Touch: Your Basic Attacks decrease Enemy Hero Attack Speed by 3% for 3s, stacking up to 4 times.
- Glacier: Permanently Gain 1 Increased Magical Armor per every 300 total gold earned.
- Diamond Tip: Gain 4% increased Physical Penetration and Magical Penetration per finished item.

Description: Imperious entities of astral lineage, celebrated for their terrifying grandeur and their command over the primordial forces of chaos and order.

Sovereigns are Best suited to Heroes looking to increase their proficiency in combat via increased ability damage and burst potential.
- Vesh: Damaging an Enemy Hero with an ability, deals 6% (+0.5% per Minute) of the damage as a DoT over 3s.

- Lich: Gain 8% (+0.5% per Level) Magical Lifesteal.
- Tithe of Death: Takedowns grant 2 Ability Haste.

- Millennia: Every 60s, increase your Ultimate Ability Damage by 1%.
- Xyris: Permanently gain 0.75% Bonus Damage per 10 Units killed.

- Furor: Entering Hero Combat grants 20% Total Attack Speed for 4s.
- Dominance: Takedowns heal you for 50 (+15% Missing Health).
- Iron Will: Heal for 12% of the damage dealt by your Critical Strikes.

- Eviscerate: Deal +20% Bonus Damage to targets who are above 85% Health.

Description: Radiant entities known for their unyielding preservation and transcendent aura, standing as the bastions of absolute light against the encroachment of the void

Divines are best suited to Heroes that thrive on miraculous empowerment & general utility, be that for sustaining and enhancing themselves, or their allies.
- Exarch: Healing or Shielding a target (including yourself) grants them 10% Total Attack Speed and empowers their Basic Attacks to deal 10% bonus Magical Damage On-Hit for 4s.

- Illumination: Gain Health Regeneration equal to your Bonus Mana Regeneration.
- Preservation: Any Healing or Shielding you receive is increased by 15%.
- Revelation: Casting an Ability decreases current Basic Ability Cooldowns by 0.3s.

- Fervour: Your Basic Attacks against Enemy Heroes restore 2 (+0.5 per level)(+6% Magical Power) Health to Yourself and Allied Heroes within 1000 units.
- Omnipresent: Gain 8% Movement Speed when out of combat.
- Delayed Fate: 25% of the Ability Damage you take is stored and dealt to yourself as a DoT effect over 3s instead.

Description: Enigmatic entities known for their unconventional manipulation of reality, often evoking confusion and paranoia in those who dare oppose them.

Anomalies are best suited to any Hero looking to defy conventional logic, enhancing them with a broad range of unconventional, specialized effects.
- Demiurge: Increase Stats gained from Items (Not including Passive Effects/Crests) by 15%, and damage dealt by Items Effects by 12%.

- Tri-Core: Deal 6% Bonus Damage On-Hit, with its damage type randomly choosing from Physical, Magical and True Damage each attack.
- Bloatware: Gain +1% Increased Damage and +1% Damage Reduction for each Item owned.
- Bio-Mechanical Fusion: Gain +1 Physical Power for every 5 Magical Power you possess.

- Cursed Corrupted: Convert every 1% Critical Strike Chance into 1 Ability Haste. (This causes you to lose the Critical Chance Stat you buy.)
- Memory Leak: On Ability Cast, Gain 6% of the Mana Cost as Permanent Maximum Mana. Upon gaining 600 Maximum Mana, permanently gain +5% Movement Speed.
